title: Kubeia
subtitle: A narrative roguelike dungeon crawler set in Greek mythology, where every roll of the dice can decide a hero's fate

world.intro: Gods, monsters and mortals share a world where fate is real — but not fixed, if you have courage, cunning, and a little luck with the dice. Each hero faces their own labyrinth: a mythological trial reinterpreted as a dungeon, one that is as narrative and emotional as it is physical. The creatures you meet are rarely simple obstacles — they are reflections of something more tragic, more human.
world.tagline: The dice are cast. The gods are watching.

stories.synopsis: King Minos demands his tribute: fourteen young Athenians delivered to the Minotaur. Theseus volunteers to end the slaughter — but the deeper he goes, the more the Minotaur looks like the victim of a curse he never chose.
After the fall of Troy, Odysseus's crew is turned to swine by a sorceress who is more than she appears. Protected by Hermes, he alone must find his way through her palace to free them.
Eurydice is dead. Inconsolable, Orpheus descends into Hades's realm, charming its guardians with his music to plead for her return.

heroes.intro: Fixed stats, a signature weapon, two abilities fuelled by the Favor of the Gods — no character creation, just a hero to become.

list.name: Theseus
list.quote: A daring warrior braving the Labyrinth in order to slay the Minotaur.
list.description: A direct, resilient fighter who meets every threat head-on — built to absorb mistakes and punish openings.

list.name: Odysseus
list.quote: A cunning hero who needs to find his way through Circe's palace to free his comrades.
list.description: Versatile and sharp-witted, leaning on deception and exploiting the enemy's every weakness.

list.name: Orpheus
list.quote: A resolute poet who descends into the Underworld to rescue his beloved Eurydice.
list.description: Fragile in a fight, magnetic everywhere else — his lyre turns charisma into sustained, aching damage.

narrative-exploration.title: Narrative exploration
narrative-exploration.description: Like a poet before his audience, we weave every room in prose. Your choices ripple forward — all the way to which ending you earn.

characters.title: Character choice
characters.description: Step into the sandals of a hero from Greek myth. Fixed attributes, a signature weapon and two Favor-powered abilities define how you play — no character creation, just a role to embody.

turn-based-combat.title: Turn-based combat
turn-based-combat.description: Some encounters can only be resolved at sword's point. Initiative, standard attacks, Favor-fuelled abilities, or a desperate flight — round after round, the dice decide between victory and death; perhaps your own.

player-progression.title: Character progression
player-progression.description: The rooms you explore hide dangers, but also lost relics and equipment. What you find — and what you give up to wear it — is yours to decide.

random-generation.title: Randomly-generated environment
random-generation.description: Each attempt has its own path to discover: the gods are capricious and enjoy rolling the dice of your destiny as you go through another trial.

screenshots.caption: Create an account or play the game straight away
Choose your character and step into their own universe

highlights.text: Just want a quick session? No account needed — jump straight into a 20 to 30 minute run.
Want to track your progress? Register with just a username and an email address to save your run history and unlocked endings.
Roll D4 to D20 in mechanics inspired by tabletop role-playing games, through a labyrinth of 10 to 15 hand-illustrated rooms that reshuffles every run.
Not satisfied with how it ended? Death regenerates the whole labyrinth — rewrite your destiny as many times as you like.

roadmap.text: Background music and audio narration, from a modernised Epitaph of Seikilos to combat percussion.
Play as Odysseus and Orpheus in their own myths — The Palace of Circe and The Underworld — as paid campaigns.
roadmap.alt: A portrait of Orpheus and Odysseus
